text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"A synthesis of meta-analyses reports that the own-wage employment elasticity of minimum wage increases is consistently modest.","cited_pids":["3ed11781c282#1","3ed11781c282#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Corrected minimum wage employment estimates, after accounting for publication bias, generally approach zero.","cited_pids":["3ed11781c282#1","3ed11781c282#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"An IESE analysis of US data from 2010 to 2016 finds that in concentrated labor markets a minimum wage hike can raise employment.","cited_pids":["cb6fd29ac7f5#1","cb6fd29ac7f5#3","cb6fd29ac7f5#4"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"The IESE analysis finds that in labor markets with many employers the minimum wage effect on employment is neutral or slightly negative.","cited_pids":["cb6fd29ac7f5#1","cb6fd29ac7f5#3","cb6fd29ac7f5#4"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"A Spanish machine-learning study covering 2001 to 2021 reports that minimum wage increases were consistent with higher net employment.","cited_pids":["6bc17d95795b#1"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"The Employment Policies Institute states that the majority of research over three decades finds minimum wage increases reduce employment.","cited_pids":["4314fdf0529f#0"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"The Employment Policies Institute is an advocacy-linked organization with a policy stake in the minimum wage debate.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c8","text":"Overall, the weight of the evidence points to small or near-zero employment effects from minimum wage increases.","cited_pids":[]}]}
